derivation.onset: Record reports no ICANS and no qualifying finding exists, so section 7.9(b) applies. Formal Grade 0 assessments exist (Day +1, Day +7), but the observation window also holds a documented 'not assessable' period (Days +8, +9: 'unable to assess'), so 7.9(b)/A21 gives 7.4 rather than 7.7.
derivation.max_grade: Same rule, section 7.9(b) and A21: because of the documented not-assessable period the 'no ICANS' record cannot be confirmed, so the grade is also 7.4. The Day +5 'confused' is an ungradeable symptom; it does not change the outcome (section 7 introduction, A21).

ambiguity_notes: The unsigned dietitian note (D04) is ignored (A27). Day +5 'confused this PM' with T 37.9 meets no Table 6 criterion and has no ICE (ungradeable neurological symptom, not a qualifying finding). Propofol sedation and intubation are mentioned together with an explicit statement that assessment was not possible, so the not-assessable period counts (A7). If a clinician judged that sedation alone does not count, the result would be 7.7, but the note does state 'unable to assess'. No further competing reading.
